story.title: I build the tools I wish existed, then I ship them.
story.p1: I'm Girgis, a self-taught developer from Egypt, now based in São Paulo. I started the way many developers do: with a problem I wanted gone and nobody to build the fix for me. So I learned to build it myself.
story.p2: That became a habit. Find a slow, manual job and replace it with something that runs on its own. Since 2021 the habit has grown into web automation, systems built for real businesses, and Android apps that are live on Google Play.
story.p3: Moving to Brazil brought new problems to solve. I needed Portuguese, so I built Lu Lingo and Gesr. I needed consulate and immigration appointments that rarely opened, so I built watchers that told my phone the moment one did.
story.p4: Today I build the same way for clients: start from the real problem, ship something that works, and keep it working.

h1.title: Real problems first
h1.text: I start from the job that is slow or broken today, not from a technology I want to try.

h2.title: Shipped, then maintained
h2.text: My apps get updates and store-policy fixes long after launch. Done means live, and still working.

h3.title: Reviewed and tested
h3.text: I use modern tools, AI-assisted development included, and I review and test everything myself before it ships.

h4.title: One person, the whole way
h4.text: Design, build, publishing and support, handled by one person who knows every part of the project.

process.title: How a project goes
process.sub: Simple and in the open, from the first message to after launch.

p1.title: You tell me the problem
p1.text: On WhatsApp, email or the contact form, in English, Portuguese or Arabic. A short description is enough to start.

p2.title: I propose a plan
p2.text: What I would build, what you get at the end, and the price and timing for your case, before any work starts.

p3.title: I build in small steps
p3.text: You see working versions along the way and can change direction early, not at the end.

p4.title: Launch, then support
p4.text: I deploy or publish it, hand over the code and instructions, and stay available for fixes and updates.

resume.summary: Developer who turns slow, manual work into software that runs itself: browser and data automation in Python and TypeScript, bilingual web platforms, and Flutter apps that are live on Google Play. I own the whole path, from design to release and maintenance.

job1.title: Automation Developer, independent
job1.b1: Built a large-scale distributed web-automation platform in TypeScript: one live dashboard driving agents on several machines, with checkpoints that resume runs at the exact step.
job1.b2: Built read-only appointment watchers with Playwright and phone alerts; one alone made 6,022 checks, and four appointments were booked.
job1.b3: Built a local Python pipeline that turns a written script into a finished 1080p animated video with narration and lip-sync.
job1.b4: Built Excel and file-processing tools and desktop apps, and replaced slow browser flows with direct HTTP requests.

job2.title: Full-stack web & mobile developer, independent
job2.b1: Lu Lingo: a 9-language app for Arabic speakers with 53,057 words, subscriptions and cloud backup, live on Google Play.
job2.b2: House of Amría: a bilingual store for an Egyptian cotton brand, built on Laravel, then rebuilt on Next.js; delivered to the client.
job2.b3: Structure ERP (with Simon): a multi-tenant ERP across 12 business areas, in Arabic and English; in development.
job2.b4: StitchHub and a WhatsApp store bot: systems delivered to a workshop and a clothing shop, each with a dashboard.
job2.b5: Published and maintain four apps on Google Play, and shipped the Android 16 and Billing 8 upgrade on time for five apps (four public, one in closed testing).

short.title: The short version
short.p1: This site has no ads, no analytics and no tracking cookies. I only receive what you choose to send me.

device.title: Saved on your device
device.p1: Your language and light or dark theme are saved in your browser (local storage) so the site remembers them. They never leave your device, and you can clear them in your browser settings.

form.title: The contact form
form.p1: When you send the form, your name, email, project type, budget and message are delivered to my email through Web3Forms, a form-delivery service. If the form is not available, your own email app sends the message instead.
form.p2: I use these details only to reply to you. I don't sell or share them, and I delete conversations that don't lead anywhere.

chat.title: The chat assistant
chat.p1: The chat bubble is an automated assistant, not me in person. Your messages go to my small server and to an AI language-model provider only to write the answer; that provider may keep them under its own privacy policy.
chat.p2: Conversations are not saved by me. Please don't share passwords, ID numbers or other sensitive data in the chat.

third.title: Other services
third.p1: Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, so Google receives your IP address when the page loads. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which keeps standard server logs.
third.p2: Links to Google Play, GitHub, LinkedIn and WhatsApp take you to those services, under their own privacy policies.

rights.title: Questions or deletion
rights.p1: Write to gogy.bairy@gmail.com and I will tell you what I have about you, or delete it.
